remainingFindings.summary: The tag-removal fix makes every untagged row's PATCH send `labels: []`, so the mirror now wipes any label applied to a BUGS item out of band (e.g. by plane-apply) the next time any other field changes.
remainingFindings.detail: Verified in this session: `resolveLabelIdsForTags` (plane-sync.mjs:626-641) now returns `[]` for a row with no tags, and the patch body spreads `...(labels ? { labels } : {})` (plane-sync.mjs:866-878), so `labels: []` is sent on EVERY patch of an untagged row — not only on the one patch that follows a tag removal. Failure scenario: an operator (or `plane-apply.mjs`, which sets `body.labels = resolveLabelIds(...)` at L173 and L219) puts a triage label such as `needs-repro` on BUGS item for B300 (an untagged registry row); later the registry row's title/state/priority changes, plane-sync issues its normal one patch for that row, and the body carries `labels: []`, dropping `needs-repro`. `plane-intake.mjs:150` reads `item.labels` as meaningful data, so labels are not decorative in this workspace. The finding this fix answered only required clearing when the row previously had labels (its fixHint: "send `labels: []` when the row's tag set is empty (or when it previously had labels)"); the shipped version is the broader reading and takes ownership of the whole label set on untagged rows. NOT fully verified: I did not find a committed ops file that labels a BUGS item today, so this is a capability-level regression rather than an observed data loss — no fake-server check in plane-sync.self-test.mjs covers "untagged row + pre-existing Plane labels" (the new T8 removal case starts from a row the mirror itself tagged).
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either scope the `[]` to the removal case (only send it when the item's current label set is non-empty AND the previous registry hash carried tags — the existing item is already fetched in `existingItems`), or document in the plan/R8 that the mirror owns the BUGS label set outright and add a self-test case pinning that an untagged row with pre-existing Plane labels is intentionally cleared.

remainingFindings.summary: Build plan still specifies the old "key omitted otherwise" label rule that the accepted fix deliberately replaced, so plan and code now disagree in three places.
remainingFindings.detail: The plane-sync fix changed the contract from "omit the `labels` key unless at least one tag resolves" to "`labels: []` when the row has no tags, key omitted only when tags exist but none resolve" (implemented at plane-sync.mjs:614-641 with an explanatory comment, and proven by the new check `T8 (R8): dropping a row's last tag patches labels to [] so the stale label goes`, which I ran green). The plan was not updated with it: L218 still reads "include `labels: [ids]` only when at least one resolves (key omitted otherwise, mirroring the 'omitted when empty' convention from R1)", L44's R8 statement and acceptance criterion 6 at L322 carry the same wording, and the embedded pipeline-args brief at L433 says "labels key on payload when non-empty". A later session reading R8/criterion 6 as the contract would read `labels: []` on every untagged patch as a bug and revert it — exactly the drift that produced the original finding. (The two line-number findings in this file are fixed: L112 now records the corrected `campaign-check.mjs` reference and I confirmed that file is 978 lines; L214 now cites `plane-client.mjs` L557, which is where `async function resolveLabels` is declared.)
remainingFindings.fixHint: Update R8 (L44), the TP brief (L216-218), acceptance criterion 6 (L322) and the pipeline-args brief (L433) to state the three-outcome rule actually shipped: `[]` for a row with no tags, resolved ids when any tag resolves, key omitted only when a row's tags all fail to resolve.
